title: ～に見える — “look ～ / appear ～”
summary: に見える describes how something looks to you: its appearance gives that impression. A noun or na-adjective takes に; an i-adjective takes く (若く見える); and ～そうに見える adds the idea of “looks as if it would ～.”

patterns.form: 名詞 ＋ に ＋ 見える
patterns.gloss: 羊に見える / 学生に見える

patterns.form: い形容詞〜く／な形容詞〜に ＋ 見える
patterns.gloss: 若く見える / 元気に見える / 忙しそうに見える

body.p: The verb 見える means “be visible, appear.” ～に見える therefore means “look like ～.” An i-adjective takes the adverbial く form, and na-adjectives and nouns take に.
Use it to give an impression from appearance: 彼女はとても若く見えます, あの雲は羊に見える, その店はいつも忙しそうに見える. It describes how things look, not facts.
～みたいだ and ～ようだ guess from looks or circumstances, while ～に見える focuses on the impression of appearance. ～そうだ (appearance) is similar but speaks of what seems about to happen.

examples.ja: 彼女（かのじょ）はとても若（わか）く見（み）えます。
あの雲（くも）は羊（ひつじ）に見（み）える。
examples.romaji: Ano kumo wa hitsuji ni mieru.
examples.tr: That cloud looks like a sheep.

examples.ja: その店（みせ）はいつも忙（いそが）しそうに見（み）える。
examples.romaji: Sono mise wa itsumo isogashisō ni mieru.

pitfalls: An i-adjective takes く: 若く見える, not 若に見える.
Do not confuse it with 見る. 見える means “can be seen, looks like.”
